'''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in {{ill|Jōyō, Kyoto|en|Jōyō, Kyoto|qid=Q817276|lt=Joyo, Kyoto}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|qid=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}.

== Overview ==
Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurumazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11369464}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park.

While originally a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique<ref name="Joyo City Tourism Association"/>.

The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}<ref name="Joyo City Tourism Association">[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).</ref>. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|qid=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}.

The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1)<ref name="National Historic Site"/> and its grave goods were Historic Site1 National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} in 1990 (Heisei 2)<ref name="National Historic Site"/>.

== Excavation History ==
* '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education<ref name="National Historic Site"/>.
* '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6<ref name="National Historic Site"/>.
* '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} on June 29<ref name="National Historic Site"/>.
* '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries<ref name="National Historic Site"/>.

== burial goods ==
[[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]]
[[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]]
Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}:
* '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror).
* '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set).
* '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces.
* '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces.
* '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces.
* '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece.
Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)<ref name="Joyo City Tourism Association"/>.

=== National Historic Site ===
* '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}</ref>.

== Related Facilities ==

'''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|qid=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} Kofun located in Terada Ōtani, {{ill|Jōyō, Kyoto|en|Jōyō, Kyoto|qid=Q817276|lt=Jōyō, Kyoto}}, Kyoto Prefecture. It is a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} and types part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群}}. This kofun has been Historic Site1 a National Historic Site, and its excavated burial goods are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}.

== Overview ==

Shibagahara Kofun was built atop a hill in the northern part of Jōyō City, southern Kyoto Prefecture. It is part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群}}, specifically the Shibagahara subgroup (Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun). An excavation in 1986 preceded the area's residential development, and the site has since been maintained as a historical park.<ref name="Historic Park">{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}.</ref>

This tomb is a keyhole-shaped mound with square front and rear mounds; however, the front portion has been leveled (current remaining length: 21 meters).<ref>{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}.</ref> The mound shows no signs of terracing, nor does it feature any {{ill|Fukiishi|fr|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|zh|葺石|qid=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi}}. Surrounding the mound is a {{ill|moat|ja|周溝}}.<ref>{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}.</ref> The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin buried directly in the ground. The coffin measures 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width, while the burial pit is 4.7 meters long and 2.5 meters wide.<ref>{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}.</ref> Numerous grave goods, including a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|qid=Q1041984|lt=bronze mirror}}, bronze bracelets, and jewels, were recovered from the coffin. Among these, the bronze bracelets are particularly rare examples.<ref name="Joyo City">{{Harvid|Joyo City Official Page}}.</ref>

The tomb was constructed in the mid-3rd century (or the early 3rd century according to some sources) during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}.<ref name="Joyo City" /> It predates the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|qid=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} and is considered one of the most significant Kofuns of its era in the southern Yamashiro region.<ref>{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}.</ref>

The kofun was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 1989, with its grave goods receiving National Important designation1 status in 1990.<ref name="Cultural designation1s"/> In 2016, the broader {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群}}, encompassing four additional kofun, was also Historic Site1 a National Historic Site.<ref name="Agency of Cultural Affairs">{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf "Regarding the designation1 of Historic Sites"]}} (Agency of Cultural Affairs press release, June 17, 2016).</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Notice No. 144, October 3, 2016.</ref> However, Shibagahara Kofun itself is not included in this extended Historic Site.

== Archaeological History ==

* 1986 (Shōwa 61): Excavation by the Jōyō City Board of Education.<ref name="Cultural designation1s"/>
* 1989 (Heisei 1): Designated a National Historic Site on September 6.<ref name="Cultural designation1s"/>
* 1990 (Heisei 2): burial goods Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} on June 29.<ref name="Cultural designation1s"/>
* 2012 (Heisei 24): Additional area Historic Site1 as part of the historic site.<ref name="Cultural designation1s"/>

== Mound area ==

The mound’s area are as follows:<ref>{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}.</ref>
* Rear mound
** North-south: 21 meters
** East-west: 19 meters
* Front mound
** Length: Approximately 3.5 meters
* Neck portion
** Width: 11.6 meters

== burial goods ==

[[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Four-animal mirror}}{{small|Exhibited at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum.}}]]
[[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze bracelet}}]]
Key burial goods recovered from the wooden coffin include:<ref>{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}</ref><ref>{{Harvid|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}.</ref>
* Four-animal bronze mirror (仿製鏡) – Diameter: 12 cm
* Two bronze bracelets (同笵)
* Eight jadeite magatama
* 187 jasper tubular beads
* 1,276 glass beads
* One yari-ganna (adze)
Additionally, fragments of {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器}}, including double-rimmed jars and high-footed bowls, were found in the gravel layer above the burial pit.<ref>{{Harvid|Kyoto Prefectural Archaeological Reports 104|2007|pp=36–37}}</ref> These burial goods are preserved and displayed at the Jōyō City History and Folklore Museum.<ref name="Joyo City" />
